memos.headline: JPM Near 52-Week Highs With Best Relative Strength; GOOGL and CAT Deteriorating
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. JPM stands out as the strongest name—just 0.6% off its 52-week high, +22.7% over 12 weeks, and leading SPY by nearly 17 points on a 12-week relative basis, all with the lowest ATR (1.70%) in the group. MSFT has surged +25.8% in four weeks and sits 20% above its 50-day mean with RSI at 70.9, which screams short-term exhaustion even though the trend is undeniably strong; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50-day before adding. On the weak side, GOOGL is down 10.8% over 12 weeks with relative strength vs SPY at -16.6% over the same period and sits 14.1% off its high—this is a broken intermediate trend. CAT is the deepest drawdown in the group at -19.6% from its 52-week high, below its 50-day mean by 6.1%, and losing to SPY on every timeframe; I'd avoid until it reclaims 900.

views.note: Sitting 0.6% from 52w high with +16.9% 12w relative strength vs SPY and low 1.70% ATR; would reassess on a close below 345.
Trend is powerful (+25.8% in 4w, +21.3% rel strength) but RSI 70.9 and 20% above 50d mean signal near-term overextension; would get long on a pullback toward 450.
Only 4.5% off 52w high, RSI 63 is healthy, and 4w relative strength vs SPY is +6.6%; would exit below 205 (200d area).
Down 10.8% over 12w with -16.6% relative strength vs SPY, RSI 47, and 14.1% drawdown—broken intermediate trend; would reconsider above 365.
Deepest drawdown in the universe at -19.6%, 6.1% below 50d mean, and losing to SPY on 4w and 12w; needs to reclaim 900 to change my view.
Worst 4w relative strength in the group at -12.8% vs SPY, RSI 43.7 drifting lower, and 10% off highs; would reconsider on a close above 320.
Trading below both 50d and 200d means, -9.2% over 26w, and 13.5% off highs—persistent underperformance with no sign of a base forming.
Short-term bounce (+4.6% 1w, +8.6% 4w) is encouraging but 12w return is still -1.5% and 12w relative strength is -7.3%; watching for follow-through above 165.
Massive 26w gain of +45.2% keeps the longer trend intact but 4w relative strength is -10.2% and RSI 42.4 suggests a correction is underway; wait for stabilization near 390.
Above both moving averages and RSI is neutral at 53.5, but 12w relative strength of -4.5% and a sharp -4.3% weekly drop warrant caution; support near 250.

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech earnings power surging; XOM and PG show cash-flow compression that warrants caution
memos.body: I am struck by the breadth of earnings acceleration across the large-cap tech complex this quarter. GOOGL posted a 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue with net income up nearly 298% YoY—likely driven by a large one-time gain, but even adjusting for that the top-line growth of 24.2% on minimal debt ($14.8B) is impressive. NVDA continues to print extraordinary numbers: $81.6B in quarterly revenue (+85% YoY) at a 71.5% net margin with only $8.5B of total debt, giving it the cleanest balance sheet relative to earnings in the universe. On the other side, XOM's net income fell 46% YoY to $4.2B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing net margin to just 4.9%, and PG saw net income decline 16% on anemic 1.5% revenue growth—neither profile suggests durable earnings power at current levels. I would need to see XOM's Q2 filing and PG's margin trajectory stabilize before getting constructive on either name.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, 71.5% net margin, and only $8.5B debt make this the highest-quality earnings stream in the universe; I would reassess if margins compress below 60%.
Full-year 10-K shows $90B quarterly revenue (+17.7% YoY), 39.7% net margin, and net income +31% with moderate $40B debt—durable cloud-driven earnings growth.

Revenue +24% YoY to $119.8B with a 93.7% net margin (likely includes a large non-operating gain) and minimal leverage at $14.8B debt; need to parse the one-time items but underlying top-line momentum is strong.
Net income exploded +245% YoY to $62.7B on $200.6B revenue, lifting net margin to 31.2%; the $133B debt load is the main risk but operating leverage is clearly inflecting.
Revenue +24% and net income +65% YoY with a healthy 17.5% net margin show strong cyclical momentum; I would turn cautious if order backlog or revenue growth decelerates below mid-single digits.
Revenue +16% and net income +27% are solid, but $82.3B in total debt and a 27.2% net margin leave less room for upside surprise versus peers; would upgrade on services mix improvement.
Net income +41% YoY to $21.2B is strong but the 36.9% margin sits on $460.5B of total debt, and bank earnings are inherently cyclical; credit quality trends in the next quarter will be decisive.
Revenue essentially flat (+0.4% YoY) at $112B with a thin 4.9% net margin and $73.3B debt; the 61% net income rebound suggests a low base, not structural improvement.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on barely growing revenue (+2.4%) with a 4.9% net margin signals commodity-driven cash-flow compression; need to see Q2 stabilization before reconsidering.
Net income fell 15.8% on just 1.5% revenue growth, compressing net margin to 14.4%—pricing power appears exhausted and I see no near-term catalyst for margin recovery.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 3.5% YoY CPI and Rising Long Yields Favor Value over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for at least three months while having cut 75bp over the past year, and the labor market is firm with unemployment at 4.10%, down 20bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons. The problem is inflation — CPI is running 3.5% YoY as of June, well above target, which explains why the 10y yield has climbed 39bp over the past year to 4.68% and the curve has steepened modestly (10y-2y at +48bp). This combination of a tight labor market, above-target inflation, and rising long rates is hostile to long-duration growth equities and supportive of banks (steeper curve, higher NIM) and defensive staples. A downside surprise in the next CPI print (below 3.0% YoY) or a jump in unemployment above 4.3% would shift my regime call toward easing expectations and flip me more constructive on duration-sensitive tech.

views.note: Positively sloped curve at 48bp, firm employment, and elevated short rates support net interest margins for large banks.
Solid macro backdrop with firm employment supports energy demand, but rising real rates cap upside; no strong directional call.
Defensive staples benefit from a pause regime with sticky inflation allowing pricing power, and they are less rate-sensitive than growth.
Long-duration growth names face headwinds from 10y yields at 4.68% and rising 39bp YoY with no near-term easing catalyst.
Quality large-cap with cash flow resilience, but elevated long rates and paused easing cycle limit multiple expansion.
Similar duration risk as AAPL; sticky CPI and rising 10y yields argue against aggressive positioning in growth until inflation cools.
Cyclical bellwether benefits from low unemployment but rising long rates and a pause regime temper conviction on further upside.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: MSFT and AMZN Surge While AAPL and GOOGL Suffer Sharp Negative Reactions
memos.body: I am reading a clear bifurcation in market sentiment across mega-cap tech following the Q2/Q3 earnings cycle. MSFT (+15.5%) and AMZN (+15.3%) saw massive positive price reactions to their earnings 8-Ks filed 7/29 and 7/30 respectively, signaling a decisive narrative shift toward rewarding cloud/AI execution. Conversely, AAPL (-7.4%) and GOOGL (-7.1%) drew punishing reactions, suggesting crowded expectations met with disappointment—tone has turned negative and may not yet be fully washed out. CAT's +5.6% post-earnings pop on 8/4 is a quieter positive signal in industrials that deserves attention. I have lower conviction on names like NVDA and XOM where recent 8-Ks were governance/corporate actions with no earnings reaction data to anchor a sentiment read.

views.note: A +15.5% earnings-day reaction is an extraordinary positive sentiment shift that likely attracts momentum flows in the near term.
The +15.3% post-earnings move signals a major positive narrative reset; sentiment momentum should persist barring macro shocks.
A -7.4% earnings reaction indicates negative sentiment inflection; with tone turning down from previously crowded positive positioning, further downside risk remains.
The -7.1% earnings drop on 7/22 and a subsequent non-earnings 8-K on 8/10 suggest unresolved negative sentiment; I see no catalyst for a near-term tone reversal.
A solid +5.6% earnings reaction in a less-crowded industrial name suggests positive sentiment with room to run.
Modest +2.5% earnings reaction and heavy routine 8-K flow suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment; no strong directional signal.
A mild -1.9% earnings reaction alongside multiple governance filings points to tepid sentiment without a clear directional catalyst.
No earnings reaction data available—only governance 8-Ks filed in late June/early July—so I lack a sentiment anchor to take a directional view.
A modest +1.2% earnings reaction is constructive but not strong enough to signal a decisive sentiment shift.
The July 8-K covered a complex acquisition/corporate restructuring with no price reaction data; sentiment read is inconclusive.

memos.headline: Declining Policy Uncertainty and Subdued VIX Suggest Geopolitical Tail Risks Are Fading, but Oil Volatility Warrants Caution on Energy
memos.body: I see a broadly constructive geopolitical backdrop as of today: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has fallen ~18% over three months to 193.83, and the VIX has compressed to 14.63, down ~18% over the same window, signaling that markets are pricing out near-term policy shocks such as new sanctions rounds or export-control escalations. High-yield OAS at 2.71% is essentially flat month-over-month and tighter over three months, consistent with no credit-market stress from geopolitical disruption. The one wrinkle is WTI crude, which is up 4.5% in the past month to $82.77 even as it remains down ~21% over three months—this divergence could reflect short-term supply-side tightness (OPEC discipline or regional disruption) rather than a structural demand shift, and I would need to see sustained prices above $85 or a new sanctions package to turn more constructive on energy. Without concrete evidence of fresh export controls on semiconductors or a deterioration in US-China trade policy, I treat the current calm as a structural de-risking rather than a one-quarter lull, though a reversal in the EPU index above 220 would change my view.

views.note: Falling policy uncertainty and no new evidence of tightened semiconductor export controls reduce the geopolitical overhang on advanced-chip demand.
Declining EPU and stable credit spreads suggest no imminent supply-chain disruption from China policy shifts, supporting hardware-heavy names.
WTI up 4.5% m/m but still down ~21% over three months leaves the energy-security thesis ambiguous; I need sustained prices above $85 or a new sanctions catalyst.
CAT's recent Reg FD disclosure and easing policy uncertainty are mildly supportive, but global infrastructure spending is sensitive to any re-escalation in trade tensions.
Steepening yield curve (+12bp m/m on 10y-2y) and low VIX favor bank earnings; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-markets activity with no geopolitical red flags.
Consumer staples face limited direct geopolitical risk, but multiple Reg FD filings in July may signal margin guidance adjustments tied to FX or input-cost pressures.
